title: There is always another number between
summary: Keep taking the middle of a gap on the number line: you never run out of numbers.
alt: A number line segment from a to a+d with the middle points marked as the student halves the gap.

shapes.text: and we can always halve again!

steps.title: Two numbers
steps.narration: Here are two numbers on the number line, {{a|2}} and {{a+d|2}}. Is there anything between them?

steps.title: The middle number
steps.narration: Yes: the **average** \( \frac{a+b}{2} = {{a+d/2|3}} \) is exactly in the middle.

steps.title: Halve again
steps.narration: Take the middle of each half. Now there are {{2^L-1|int}} numbers between them.

steps.title: And again
steps.narration: Halving once more gives {{2^L-1|int}} numbers. The gaps get smaller but there is always a new middle.

steps.title: It never stops
steps.narration: Keep halving and you never run out. Between **any** two different numbers there are **infinitely many** rational numbers, and irrational ones too.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.narration: Change **a** and **d** and slide **L**. Try two numbers that are very close together.

formulas.title: Midpoint
formulas.text: The average of two numbers lies exactly between them.

challenges.title: Find the middle
challenges.prompt: Find the number exactly halfway between 2 and 3.

challenges.title: How many?
challenges.prompt: How many rational numbers lie between 2 and 3?
challenges.hint: Keep halving. Does it ever stop?
challenges.explain: You can always take the middle of any gap, so there are **infinitely many**.

intro: Rational numbers are packed together so tightly that no gap on the number line is ever empty.
takeaways: The midpoint of two numbers is between them.
Halving can go on for ever, so there are infinitely many numbers between any two.

notes.title: Dense
notes.text: We say the rational numbers are dense: between any two there is another.
